hypotheses.H1: Boundary cases put far more switches in the middle of the probability range than E1's labelled sets (E1: 21 of 2889 switches between p 0.1 and 0.9; 12 of 147 calls with top p < 0.9).
hypotheses.H2: The team loop is a label for cross-team boundaries and blind within a team: when the intent judgment is wrong across teams, the loop disagrees (surprise) far more often than when it is right; within a team, a wrong intent still maps to the right team, so the loop cannot see it.
hypotheses.H3: On this distribution Jev's intent switches are measurably miscalibrated somewhere in the middle range (enough mass there to estimate it), and the expected calibration error is larger than E1's 0.003.

labels: A case's label is its generation target (the intent the generator was asked to write, clearly or leaning); `even` cases have no label and are used only for confidence and resonance. Synthetic labels, not human ones.
